title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Solomon Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Solomon Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Solomon Islands: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Solomon Islands, families and executors coordinate hospital or community death notifications, civil registration under the Births and Deaths (Registration) Act 1988, claims with Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (SINPF), and statutory Will-deposit and estate timelines under the Wills, Probate and Administration Act 1987 [1][2][3][7].

steps.title: Medical certification, hospital coordination, and community notifications
steps.html:
• Obtain the official hospital Death Notification Form and medical cause-of-death record from the attending clinician at National Referral Hospital (NRH) in Honiara (+677 44000 switchboard; +677 23600 general line; +677 21068 Emergency Operations Centre) or the local provincial health facility [6][14].
  • Where burial takes place in a church or village community without a formal hospital death record, collect both the church minister's burial/death confirmation and a Statutory Declaration sworn by parents, guardians, or an immediate relative before a Magistrate or Commissioner for Oaths [3][4].
  • Keep original certified medical and burial confirmations together, as civil registration and superannuation payouts depend on primary supporting records [3][7].

steps.title: Civil death registration through the Registrar General and Home Affairs
steps.html:
• Register the death under the Births and Deaths (Registration) Act 1988 by completing the official Application for Registration of a Death (CRVS Death Form) through Ministry of Home Affairs civil registration services and Registrar General's Office (Hibiscus Avenue, Point Cruz, Honiara; P.O. Box G15; Tel +677 23002; Fax +677 23716) [1][3][4][5].
  • Attach the hospital Death Notification Form, church burial notification where applicable, the sworn Statutory Declaration of next-of-kin, and claimant identification [3][4].
  • Request multiple certified Death Certificate extracts immediately for SINPF benefit claims, court probate filings, commercial banks, and overseas diplomatic procedures [2][7][15].

steps.title: Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (SINPF) death and funeral benefit
steps.html:
• Contact Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (SINPF) (+677 21852; enquiry@sinpf.org.sb) promptly so member savings and statutory bereavement support can be processed [7][9].
  • Eligible deceased contributors carry a Special Death Benefit (SDB) of SBD 10,000 alongside total accumulated member contributions and interest paid to validly nominated beneficiaries [7].
  • Submit the SINPF Death Claim or Unclaimed Deposits form with the certified Death Certificate, Statutory Declaration or Affidavit of Next-of-Kin, marriage or birth certificates proving relationship, and two forms of valid government-issued ID [7][8].

steps.title: Mandatory 30-day Will deposit, High Court probate, Small Estates, and IRD tax
steps.html:
• Observe the strict criminal duty under Section 107 of the Wills, Probate and Administration Act 1987: any person holding a deceased person's Will must deposit it with the High Court or local Magistrate within 30 days of learning of the death (non-compliance carries a fine up to $1,000) [2].
  • Note statutory court waiting periods and land exclusions under the 1987 Act: customary land (s. 2(3)) and customary usage (s. 2(4)) are excluded from probate operation; no Grant of Probate may issue within 7 days of death and no Letters of Administration within 14 days unless urgent (s. 18); Small Estates under Part IV (ss. 54-59) can proceed via the High Court or Magistrate's Court (subject to a 90-day review period); intestate estates vest in the Public Trustee pending grant (s. 60(2), coordinated via Registrar General's Office / Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs, +677 28422); distribution follows a 1-year statutory window (s. 83), and Family Provision claims run within 6 months of grant (s. 95) [2][5].
  • Contact Inland Revenue Division (IRD) (+677 21493 Honiara Customer Service Centre, Mendana Ave, P.O. Box G9; +677 28307 Income Tax) to settle final PAYE or income tax filings; Solomon Islands has no separate inheritance or estate tax [12][13]. Check final wages and leave settlements under the Labour Act (Cap. 73) and Employment Act (Cap. 72) [10][11].

steps.title: Consular legalisation and notifying banks and institutions
steps.html:
• Because Solomon Islands is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified Death Certificates and High Court grants used overseas require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than an Apostille [16]. Confirm authentication rules with the foreign receiving mission or registry before mailing originals abroad [15][16].
  • Notify Solomon Islands banks, insurers, utilities, employers, and property offices in writing with certified Death Certificates and court grants [2][10][11].
  • Retain complete copies of Civil Registry forms, SINPF settlement letters, High Court filings, and IRD tax clearances [3][7][12].
